Looking at this complex problem, I need to track items through multiple transformations. Let me write Python code to systematically model and apply each step.

```python
from collections import Counter, defaultdict

class Item:
    def __init__(self, name, origin, size, material, smell, color):
        self.name = name
        self.origin = origin
        self.size = size
        self.material = material
        self.smell = smell
        self.color = color
    
    def copy(self):
        return Item(self.name, self.origin, self.size, self.material, self.smell, self.color)
    
    def __repr__(self):
        return f"{self.name}({self.origin}, {self.size}, {self.material}, {self.smell}, {self.color})"

# Step 0: Create initial collection of 33 items
initial_items_data = [
    ("speaker", "Polish", "large", "ceramic", "chocolate", "beige"),
    ("stapler", "Portuguese", "medium", "ceramic", "coconut", "black"),
    ("flower pot", "British", "medium", "ceramic", "garlic", "black"),
    ("speaker", "Brazilian", "medium", "plastic", "vanilla", "blue"),
    ("plate", "British", "extra-extra-large", "steel", "vinegar", "brown"),
    ("camera", "Spanish", "small", "glass", "burning wood", "crimson"),
    ("lamp", "Iranian", "extra-small", "glass", "burning wood", "cyan"),
    ("calculator", "Spanish", "extra-extra-small", "glass", "gasoline", "cyan"),
    ("scissors", "French", "extra-extra-small", "ceramic", "garlic", "cyan"),
    ("camera", "Brazilian", "extra-small", "plastic", "wet dog", "gray"),
    ("vase", "German", "small", "plastic", "leather", "green"),
    ("vase", "Iranian", "medium", "plastic", "leather", "green"),
    ("wallet", "Afghan", "small", "plastic", "baking bread", "indigo"),
    ("house", "Russian", "extra-large", "concrete", "chocolate", "indigo"),
    ("ring", "Spanish", "small", "glass", "freshly cut grass", "indigo"),
    ("bag", "Chinese", "medium", "steel", "citrus fruits", "khaki"),
    ("guitar", "Japanese", "extra-extra-large", "plastic", "rose", "khaki"),
    ("fork", "British", "extra-extra-large", "steel", "coconut", "magenta"),
    ("saw", "Spanish", "extra-small", "steel", "freshly cut grass", "magenta"),
    ("scissors", "French", "large", "concrete", "chocolate", "magenta"),
    ("stapler", "British", "extra-extra-large", "ceramic", "coffee", "pink"),
    ("necklace", "Japanese", "extra-small", "plastic", "coconut", "pink"),
    ("plier", "Japanese", "large", "plastic", "vinegar", "pink"),
    ("candle", "Afghan", "small", "concrete", "gasoline", "purple"),
    ("ball", "German", "extra-extra-small", "glass", "citrus fruits", "purple"),
    ("bicycle", "Japanese", "extra-extra-large", "steel", "garlic", "purple"),
    ("bottle", "Japanese", "extra-large", "glass", "baking bread", "red"),
    ("clock", "Italian", "extra-extra-small", "glass", "rose", "red"),
    ("pen", "Canadian", "extra-small", "concrete", "citrus fruits", "teal"),
    ("canvas", "Portuguese", "extra-extra-large", "concrete", "rose", "teal"),
    ("ruler", "Brazilian", "extra-extra-small", "glass", "burning wood", "turquoise"),
    ("bag", "French", "small", "steel", "rose", "turquoise"),
    ("banana", "Spanish", "large", "ceramic", "chocolate", "violet"),
]

items = [Item(*data) for data in initial_items_data]
initial_items_data_copy = initial_items_data.copy()

# Step 1: Cousin's gift - add copies with lavender smell for items with citrus fruits or coffee
target_smells = {"pine needles", "citrus fruits", "coffee"}
gifts = []
for item in items:
    if item.smell in target_smells:
        gift = item.copy()
        gift.smell = "lavender"
        gifts.append(gift)

items.extend(gifts)

# Step 2: Aunt's swap - replace material with plastic and smell with coconut for extra-extra-large items
for item in items:
    if item.size == "extra-extra-large":
        item.material = "plastic"
        item.smell = "coconut"

# Step 3: Dad removes items of a certain color (gray)
items = [item for item in items if item.color != "gray"]

# Step 4: Remove item types with even counts
item_type_counts = Counter(item.name for item in items)
items = [item for item in items if item_type_counts[item.name] % 2 == 1]

# Step 5: Fiancee's addition - add copies for new (smell, color) pairs
initial_smell_color_pairs = set((smell, color) for name, origin, size, material, smell, color in initial_items_data_copy)
current_smell_color_pairs = set((item.smell, item.color) for item in items)
new_pairs = current_smell_color_pairs - initial_smell_color_pairs

for new_smell, new_color in new_pairs:
    for item in items:
        if item.smell == new_smell and item.color == new_color:
            duplicate = item.copy()
            items.append(duplicate)
            break

# Step 6: Lost one extra-extra-large item
extra_large_items = [item for item in items if item.size == "extra-extra-large"]
if extra_large_items:
    items.remove(extra_large_items[0])

# Final count - items matching all criteria
count = 0
for item in items:
    if (item.color != "pink" and 
        item.size != "extra-extra-large" and 
        item.material != "glass" and 
        item.smell != "rose" and 
        item.origin != "Spanish"):
        count += 1

print(f"ANSWER: {count}")
```
